config.title: List Rendering with map()

intro.title: List Rendering with map()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays a list of items, such as a to-do list or a set of product names, using JavaScript's map() method. You will learn how to transform an array of data into a list of HTML elements dynamically, which is a fundamental concept in web development called list rendering. The main technologies involved are Vue's template syntax for rendering and JavaScript's array map() method for iteration. This approach allows your UI to automatically update when the underlying data changes, making your applications more interactive and maintainable. By the end, you'll understand how to efficiently render lists in Vue without manually writing repetitive HTML.
intro.usecase: List rendering with map() is essential for displaying dynamic data collections in real Vue applications. You'll use this pattern to render product listings in e-commerce sites, display user comments on social media platforms, and populate dashboard widgets with analytics data. Developers rely on map() to transform API response arrays into interactive UI components like search result lists, notification panels, and data tables. This approach keeps your interface synchronized with changing data while maintaining clean, maintainable code.

objectives: Initialize a reactive array in a Vue component to store list data
Apply the map() method to transform an array of raw data into a structured list
Render a dynamic list in the template using v-for with the transformed array
Bind unique keys to each list item for optimal Vue rendering performance
Manipulate list data by adding or removing items and observing reactive updates
Integrate list rendering with user interaction by handling click events on items
Configure conditional rendering within a list to display or hide specific items based on state

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary functionality from the Vue framework.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create and export a default Vue component named 'ListRenderingDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Use the Vue defineComponent API or a simple object with a setup method. The setup function should return an empty object for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue';

// Create and export a default Vue component named 'ListRenderingDemo' with a setup function
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named ListRenderingDemo is created and exported as default, with a setup function returning an empty object.
successCriteria: The component is named 'ListRenderingDemo', exported as default, has a setup function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named 'ListRenderingDemo', exported as default, has a setup function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component named 'ListRenderingDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object, and export it as default.

steps.title: Initialize reactive data array
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your ListRenderingDemo component, use ref to create a reactive array called 'items' with at least three sample objects, each having 'id' and 'name' properties.
steps.hint: Initialize the ref with an array of objects. For example: { id: 1, name: 'Item 1' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive 'items' array is created inside the setup function, ready to be used for list rendering.
successCriteria: The setup function contains a ref declaration for 'items' with an array of at least three objects, each having 'id' and 'name' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a ref, but make sure it's named 'items' and contains an array of objects with 'id' and 'name' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a reactive array called 'items' with sample data inside the setup function. Review the hint and try again.

steps.title: Define template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your Vue component with a container div element that will hold the list items.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, the template section defines the HTML structure. Add a <template> tag with a <div> inside it.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a template section in Vue
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a template section with a container div element ready to hold list items.
successCriteria: The Vue component includes a <template> section with a <div> element inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the <template> tag and a <div> element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template section with a container div is missing. Add a <template> tag with a <div> element inside.

steps.title: Add unordered list element
steps.instruction: Inside the template's div container, add an unordered list element (<ul>) that will contain your list items.
steps.hint: Add a <ul> tag inside the existing <div> in your template.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a list container in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a <ul> element ready to hold list items.
successCriteria: A <ul> element is added inside the template's <div> container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a <ul> element inside the <div> in your template.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a <ul> element inside the template's <div> container.

steps.title: Use v-for directive for list rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the unordered list element in your template, add an <li> element with the v-for directive to iterate through the items array.
steps.hint: Use v-for="item in items" on the <li> tag to loop through each element in the items array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a list with v-for
  • {{ task.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list now contains an <li> element with v-for directive ready to display array items.
successCriteria: An <li> element with v-for="item in items" is added inside the <ul> tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the v-for directive correctly on the <li> element. The syntax should be v-for="item in items".
steps.feedbackWrong: The v-for directive wasn't properly added. Remember to add an <li> element inside the <ul> with v-for="item in items" to iterate through the array.

steps.title: Display item content in list
steps.instruction: Inside each <li> element, display the item's name property using Vue's template interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output the value of item.name within the <li> tags.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a property in Vue template
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: Each list item will show the name from the corresponding array element when data is added later.
successCriteria: Each <li> element contains {{ item.name }} inside its tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct syntax {{ item.name }} inside the <li> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list items aren't displaying the name property. Check that you're using Vue's template interpolation syntax correctly.

steps.title: Add unique key binding
steps.instruction: In the template, add the :key binding to the <li> element using item.id to provide a unique identifier for each list item.
steps.hint: Use Vue's :key directive with the item's id property to ensure efficient list updates.
steps.analogousExample: • {{ task.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The list items will now have proper key bindings for Vue's efficient virtual DOM updates.
successCriteria: The <li> element includes :key="item.id" binding in the v-for directive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using :key="item.id" on the <li> element within the v-for loop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The key binding isn't quite right. Remember to add :key="item.id" to the <li> element to give each item a unique identifier.

steps.title: Add new item handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named 'addNewItem' that pushes a new item object to the 'items' array.
steps.hint: Create a regular JavaScript function that uses the 'items' array from your ref and the array's push method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'addNewItem' is defined in the setup function, ready to modify the reactive items array.
successCriteria: The 'addNewItem' function is defined and uses the push method to add a new item object to the 'items' array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named 'addNewItem' and actually pushes a new item object to the 'items' array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named 'addNewItem' inside the setup function that modifies the 'items' array.

steps.title: Add button to trigger handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template's div (after the unordered list) that uses the @click directive to call the addNewItem handler function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the closing tag. Use @click="addNewItem" to connect the click event to your handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler in Vue
<button @click="handleClick">Add Item</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a button that, when clicked, will trigger the addNewItem function to add new items to the list.
successCriteria: A button element is present in the template with @click="addNewItem" attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing the @click directive or the correct handler name. Make sure to use @click="addNewItem" to connect the button to your handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with @click handler is missing or incorrect. Add a button after the unordered list with @click="addNewItem".
